title: A New Beat on Climate for a Times Veteran
body_markdown:
David Gelles will cover the economic impacts of a warming planet. Read more from Climate editor, Lyndsey Layton, and deputy editors, Jesse Pesta and Mike Madden.


Climate change is reshaping insurance markets, agriculture, supply chains, labor productivity, real estate, facility planning and the global flow of capital and trade. It is a central force reordering how industries make decisions and compelling societies to make difficult choices about how to spend scarce resources. It is pulsing through economies, but often goes unrecognized.


We’re thrilled to announce that David Gelles will take on a new beat to cover all of this and more.


David, who joined the Climate desk in 2022 after nine years writing for Business, has the right background, skillset and passion to reveal the economic impacts of a warming planet.


His mandate will span everything from how outerwear manufacturers account for warmer winters to how ports are redesigned for rising seas. He’ll find those who invested in a once-stable climate that is fast-changing and shifting the ground beneath them. And he’ll look for the people and companies that are profiting from a changing climate and how they use power and money to maintain their advantage.


David will continue his role as the maestro behind Climate Forward, our successful live journalism event, which has become a buzzy annual highlight of New York Climate Week. He will also continue to represent the Climate team at global news events like Davos.


David is an


indefatigable


reporter and fluid writer. And he is a shapeshifter; he easily switches formats, toggling between “The Great Read” and “Times Insider” while contributing to The Times Magazine and making appearances on “The Daily.


”


In the space of hours, David can produce a pitch-perfect piece about Dolly Parton’s philanthropy or the death of climate economist William D. Nordhaus.


Above all, he is collaborative and affable, someone who is happy to team up with colleagues and brings a can-do spirit to new challenges.


On Climate,


David


has chronicled the complicated relationship between the corporate world and climate action. Last year, he was part of the team that was a Gerald Loeb Award finalist for


“


[Power Moves](https://www.nytimes.com/series/power-moves) ,” our series examining China’s drive to dominate clean energy.


As a reporter for Business, he was part of the team that


covered the Boeing 737 Max crashes with a mix of investigations and breaking news, work that won a Loeb in 2020. In 2017, he relaunched the Corner Office column, interviewing more than 100 business and cultural leaders and expanding the franchise with live events. Before The Times, David covered Wall Street for The Financial Times, where he interviewed Bernie Madoff in prison.


He is the author of three books, including last year’s “Dirtbag Billionaire,” which grew out of his


[huge Times scoop](https://www.nytimes.com/2022/09/14/climate/patagonia-climate-philanthropy-chouinard.html) about Yvon Chouinard, the founder of Patagonia, and how he gave away his fortune to fight climate change.


David graduated from Boston University and has a master’s in journalism from the University of California, Berkeley, Graduate School of Journalism.


Please join us in congratulating David on this exciting new role.


— Lyndsey, Jesse and Mike
